questions.text: Events JSON They're coming in. Kinesis Data Firehose and are delivered to S3 for consultation with Athena. The queries are expensive and slow because the files are JSON The team wants the data already CHEGUEM to S3 in column format, without adding components. Which configuration resolves?
options: Change Firehose to DMS
Enable the format conversion of Firehose itself to Apache Parquet, using a Glue Catalogue Date
Increase Firehose buffer to 900 seconds
Create a cluster EMR to convert files after delivery
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: DMS is bank migration, no streaming delivery. B) Correct: Firehose converts JSON→Parquet/ORC In the case of the product concerned, the data are used in the same way as for the product concerned. Athena. C) Incorrect: larger buffer changes file size, not format. D) Incorrect: works, but adds cluster and cost, violating requirement.

questions.text: A stream of the Kinesis Data Streams in Provisioned Mode suffers ProvidedThroughputExceededException at peak times, and the traffic pattern is unpredictable. What change eliminates manual capacity management?
options: Add a second identical stream
Change partition key to constant value
Migrate stream to mode ON-DEMAND, automatically dimensioning capacity
Reduce retention period
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: duplicate streams divides the architecture and does not solve the root. B) Incorrect: constant key creates A hot shard and worsens everything. C) Correct: on-demand shards scale mode automatically according to traffic — ideal for unpredictable loads. D) Incorrect: retention affects storage/replay, not write limit.

questions.text: A daily job of the AWS Glue reprocessed TODOS the historical files of a prefix of the S3 to each execution, increasing cost and duration. Which feature makes the job process only new data since the last execution?
options: Enable Bucket Version
Glue Job Bookmarks
Glue Registration Scheme
Increase DPU number
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: versioning protects objects, does not control the scope of the job. B) Correct: bookmarks track what has already been processed (archives/partitions), making the executions incremental. C) Incorrect: Schedule Registry versiona streaming schemes. D) Incorrect: more DPUs accelerate unnecessary reprocessing — the cost continues.

questions.text: Business analysts SEM Spark knowledge need to clean and standardize spreadsheets (remove duplicates, standardize dates, treat null) with a visual interface, before making them available in the data lake.?
options: AWS Lambda with pandas
Amazon EMR with notebooks
AWS Glue DataBrew, with visual transformations ready
Write PySpark jobs in Glue Study
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: Lambda with pandas is pure code and has time/memory limits. B) Incorrect: notebooks EMR require code and cluster. C) Correct: DataBrew offers 250+ visual transformations (profile, cleaning, normalization) without writing code, generating reusable recipes. D) Incorrect: requires Spark code — audience is analyst without code.

questions.text: An Oracle on-premises bank migration to the AWS It needs downtime of a few minutes. The bank receives continuous writing. AWS DMS enable it?
options: Full load unique at the weekend
Full load + CDC (change data capture), replicating the changes continuously until the time of the cutter
Export dump SQL and import manually
Snapshot of the restored storage in AWS
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: a single full load loses the writings that occur during and after loading. B) Correct: the DMS load everything and then apply the changes in almost real time (CDC) — the cutover only turns the point of the application. C) Incorrect: dump/import generates hours of unavailability. D) Incorrect: storage snapshot is not portable between machines/managed environments..

questions.text: A Spark job runs 2 hours per night. Today the cluster EMR It's on. 24/7 "to ensure." Which architecture change drastically reduces the cost by keeping the job running?
options: Move HDFS for larger volumes
Schedule the job for business hours
Adopt clusters TRANSIENTES: create the cluster for the job (data no S3 way EMRFS) and close it automatically at the end
Fold the size of the knots to the job finish faster
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: HDFS higher increases cost and links the data to the cluster. B) Incorrect: the time does not change the 24c) Correct: with data on S3 (EMRFS), the cluster becomes disposable — only the ~2D) Incorrect: we increase the cost per hour.

questions.text: A team needs to calculate aggregations in windows of 1 minute (e.g. total sales per minute) on a stream of Kinesis EM TEMPO REAL, sending the results to dashboards. Which service performs this continuous processing with status and windows?
options: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
Amazon Athena
AWS Glue Crawler
Amazon QuickSight
questions.explanation: A) Correct: o Managed Flink (ex-Kinesis Data Analytics) processes streams with time windows, status and SQL/Java/Python — the case of exact use.: Athena consult data at rest in S3, no streams on the move. C) Incorrect: Crawler catalog metadata. D) Incorrect: QuickSight view; does not process streams.

questions.text: Producers publish Avro events in a topic and the schemes evolve frequently, breaking consumers. VALIDAR and VERSIONAR the schemas centrally, controlling the compatibility of the changes.?
options: Amazon S3 Versioning
AWS Glue Registration Scheme
Glue Data Quality
AWS Configure
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: versioning of the S3 is of objects, not schema contract. B) Correct: the Registry schema records and versions schemas (Avro/JSON/Protobuf) of streams, applying compatibility rules (backward/forward) in evolution. C) Incorrect: Data Quality validates the DADOS, not the evolution of the streaming scheme. D) Incorrect: Config audit resource configuration AWS.

questions.text: A pipeline records individual events on S3, generating thousands of files of few KB per day. Athena were slow even with Parquet and partitions. What is the cause and correction?
options: Athena does not support Parquet
The S3 limits the amount of files per bucket
Failure to activate the Acceleration Transfer
The problem of SMALL FILES: excessive tiny files generates overhead per object; correction is compact/group into larger files (ex.: 128 MB+) via Firehose buffer or compaction jobs
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: Parquet is the preferred format of Athena. B) Incorrect: there is no practical limit of objects per bucket. C) Incorrect: Transfer Acceleration is upload, not analytic reading. D) Correct: each file has fixed list/opening cost; millions of small files kill performance. Larger buffers in intake and periodic compaction jobs solve.

questions.text: The same stream of the Kinesis needs to feed a real-time analysis consumer and allow new consumers to reread the events of the last 7 days (reprocessing). Which configuration attends?
options: Kinesis Data Streams with extended retention for 7 days, allowing multiple consumers and replay
Kinesis Firehose data with backup enabled
SQS Standard with DLQ
SNS with replay enabled
questions.explanation: A) Correct: Data Streams retains records (24standard h, extendable to 365 (b) Incorrect: Firehose delivers and does not allow rereading of the stream. SQS no replay. D) Wrong: SNS it's immediate push, no rereading retention.

questions.text: A company needs to move 400 TB of historical data for the S3 in 3 weeks, with internet link of 200 Mbps. Which solution meets the deadline?
options: Multipart upload parallel
AWS DataSync on the Internet
Devices AWS Snowball Edge (physical transfer)
S3 Transfer Acceleration
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: parallelism does not create extra band. B) Incorrect: DataSync optimizes, but 400 TB a ~200 Mbps would take months. ~1 week asks the Snow family; devices are sent, loaded locally and returned. D) Incorrect: acceleration via edge does not change the contracted physical band.

questions.text: A team wants to execute ETL Spark sometimes a day, SEM manage clusters and without optimizing infrastructure, accepting the cost by DPU. Another load requires custom native libraries, runtime control and specific instances with Spot. What services do they provide, respectively?
options: EMR for the first; Athena for the second
Lambda for the first; Glue for the second
AWS Glue for the first case; Amazon EMR for the second
Glue for both cases
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: Athena does not rotate ETL Arbitrary Spark with native libraries. B) Incorrect: Lambda has 15 min limit and not Spark. C) Correct: Glue = Spark serverless with minimal effort; EMR = Total control (AMIs, native libraries, fleet Spot). D) Incorrect: or Glue does not control runtime/instances/Spot required in the second case.

questions.text: No. Amazon Redshift, a table FATO giant is often united (JOIN) to a table by a client_id column, and the queries suffer with redistribution of data between us. Which distribution style minimizes this shuffle?
options: DISTSTYLE KEY in both tables, using client_id as the distribution key
DISTSTYLE EVEN in the two tables
DISTSTYLE ALL in the table fact
DISTSTYLE AUTO disabled
questions.explanation: A) Correct: KEY the MESMA join column, the corresponding lines are in the same node (co-location) and the JOIN B) Incorrect: EVEN randomly spreads, ensuring the shuffle no JOIN. C) Incorrect: ALL copy the entire table in each node — unfeasible for giant fact tables. D) Incorrect: 'deactivate the AUTO' is not a strategy.

questions.text: What is the correct use of DISTSTYLE ALL no Redshift?
options: Tables made with billions of lines
Any table with intense writing
Temporary staging tables
Small and little modified DIMENSION Tables, fully copied for all nodes to accelerate JOINS
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: replicate billions of lines in each node explodes storage. B) Incorrect: each writing replicates in all nodes — bad for intense writing. C) Incorrect: staging does not need replication. D) Correct: small dimensions (e.g. product table) in ALL are local to any JOIN, eliminating redistribution — the replicated storage cost is irrelevant to small tables.

questions.text: IB Dashboards no Redshift They're slow. APENAS on Monday mornings, when hundreds of analysts consult simultaneously. The cluster attends well the rest of the week and the team does not want to pay for a larger cluster all the time.?
options: Restart cluster on Mondays
Elastic Resize Permanent
Migrate everything to RDS
Competition Scaling, adding automatic transitory clusters at peaks of competition
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: restart does not add competition capacity.: RDS It's OLTP, no BI.D warehouse correct: the Competition Scaling adds automatic transitory capacity during peaks of simultaneous queries and removes it afterwards (with free daily credits).

questions.text: A precise start-up of data warehouse for ESPORADIC and unpredictable loads (a few hours a week), without managing cluster, paying only for the processing consumed. Redshift answer?
options: Dc2 cluster always connected
Cluster provided ra3 with reserve of 3 years
Redshift Spectrum alone, no warehouse
Amazon Redshift Serverless, charged by RPU-time during use
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: 24/7 for a few hours per week is the opposite of efficient. B) Incorrect: booking of 3 years for sporadic use waste money. C) Incorrect: Spectrum is query extension to S3 — presupposes a warehouse/endpoint Redshift. D) Correct: Serverless automatically size and charge only while there are queries — perfect for intermittent use.

questions.text: A recurring consultation of the Athena Scan 2 TB of JSON raw to generate the same aggregate cut. MATERIALIZAR this result in S3 in Parquet partitioned, using the own Athena. Which resource to use?
options: UNLOAD of the Redshift
VACUUM
A trigger from the DynamoDB
CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS), defining Parquet format and partitioning in creation
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: UNLOAD is from Redshift, (b) Incorrect: VACUUM is table maintenance (Redshift/Iceberg), non-materialization.: DynamoDB does not participate in this flow. CTAS executes the query and saves the result as a new table in S3, already in Parquet/compressed/shared — the following queries read the optimized dataset.

questions.text: The data team wants to impose a LIMITE of data scanned by reference to Athena to contain costs per team, in addition to separating the metrics of use of the marketing and financial team. Athena implements this?
options: S3 Request Country
Increase query timeout
Workgroups, with scanned and metric bytes limits per group
Athena Federated Query
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: Request Country transfers the cost of S3 to the applicant, does not limit queries. B) Incorrect: timeout does not control cost by bytes. C) Correct: workgroups isolate times, define location of results, apply data limits scanned by query (cancelling who exceeds) and publish separate metrics. D) Incorrect: Federated Query consults other sources — nothing to do with limits..

questions.text: A table of the DynamoDB needs to be analyzed with SQL complex with data lake data, SEM consumption of table reading capacity in production. What native approach attends?
options: Use native export of DynamoDB for the S3 (from PITR, without consuming RCUs) and consult with Athena
Rolling massive scans directly into the table
Transform the table into Global Table
Create read replicas from DynamoDB
questions.explanation: A) Correct: or export to S3 use continuous backup (PITR) — zero impact on the table — and the result (DynamoDB JSON/Ion) can be consulted via Athena. B) Incorrect: Massive scan consumes RCUs and threatens production. C) Incorrect: Global Tables are multi-region replication, not analysis. D) Incorrect: DynamoDB has no 'read replicas' as RDS.

questions.text: Repeative dashboard queries perform heavy aggregations always equal in Redshift. The team wants to pre-compute these results DENTRO warehouse, with managed update. Which resource to use?
options: Export to spreadsheets
Increase the number of nodes
Materialized Views, with REFRESH incremental when possible
Common Views
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: spreadsheets outside the warehouse break governance and do not scale. B) Incorrect: more we are brute force expensive for a calculation repetition problem. C) Correct: materialized views store the pre-computed result and can be updated incrementally — dashboards start reading the result ready. D) Incorrect: common views re-execute the entire query to each access.

questions.text: When comparing Apache Avro and Apache Parquet in a pipeline, what is the correct positioning of each format?
options: Both are compression formats, not file formats
Avro is columnar and Parquet is line to line
Parquet is always superior in all cases
Avro (based on LINHAS, with built-in schema) is strong for transport/streaming and schema evolution; Parquet (COLUNAR) is strong for analytical storage and queries
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: they are formats of ARQUIVO/serialization; compression (Snappy), GZIP) is orthogonal. B) Incorrect: it is the reverse. C) Incorrect: for transport record record, Avro usually is better. D) Correct: this is the classic division — Avro serializes complete records (good for Kafka/Kinesis and schema contracts); Parquet organizes by columns (good for Athena/Spectrum/Spark analytical).

questions.text: A consultation at the Redshift almost always filter by date_sale. Scans are reading too many blocks. Which choice of physical design reduces the blocks read in this pattern?
options: Use DISTSTYLE ALL
Set Date_Sale as DISTKEY
Create a B-tree Index
Set Date_Sale as SORT KEY Table
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: ALL is a small table replication, not related to the filter.: DISTKEY decides ONDE the lines stay (co-location of JOIN), (c) Incorrect: Redshift does not use B-tree indices as OLTP. D) Correct: with key sort on date_sale, the data is sorted on disk and zone metadata allows PULAR blocks outside the filter (zone maps) — minus I/O.

questions.text: A pipeline step in the Step Functions call one API unstable external. The team wants 3 new attempts with increasing interval and, if all fail, divert to a state of treatment that reports the team — TUDO without writing control code.?
options: Loop of Lambda Calling yourself
Increase state timeout
Retry Blocks (with BackoffRate and MaxAttempts) and Catch in the very state of the machine
A cron that re-executes the entire pipeline
questions.explanation: (a) Incorrect: Lambda is fragile and reinvents what the platform gives ready. B) Incorrect: major timeout does not create retentatives. C) Correct: Retry/Catch are declarative in ASL: ErrorEquals, IntervalSeconds, BackoffRate, MaxAttempts and diversion to failback states. D) Incorrect: re-execute everything because of a wasteful step and does not isolate the error.

questions.text: A flow composed of components of the Glue (crawler → cleaning job → aggregation job) needs to be chained with conditional triggers (just follow if the previous step was successful). What option keeps the orchestration DENTRO of its own Glue?
options: Call jobs manually by the console
Glue Workflows with conditional triggers
Amazon MWAA
AWS Backup
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: manual operation is not orchestration.: Glue Workflows chain crawlers and jobs with triggers (scheduled, on demand, successful/failure) and graphical view of execution — no extra service. C) Incorrect: MWAA works, but adds an external orchestrator to a flow 100% Glue. D) Incorrect: AWS Backup is backup, not orchestration.

questions.text: The nocturnal pipeline failed and no one noticed until the dashboards dawn empty. ALERTA IMEDIATO in job failures of the Glue or Step Functions?
options: Rules of EventBridge capturing failure events (job/execution) FAILED) and publishing in a topic SNS notifying the team
Increase the number of withdrawals indefinitely
Enable versioning of S3
Manually review logs every morning
questions.explanation: A) Correction: Glue and Step Functions events of change of state in the EventBridge; a rule in FAILED → SNS (E-mail/chat/on-call) closes the alert in real time. B) Incorrect: recries masked without warning — and persistent failures remain silent. C) Incorrect: versioning does not monitor anything. D) Incorrect: manual monitoring is exactly what failed.

questions.text: Before publishing a daily dataset for business, the team wants to BLOQUEAR the publication if the completion of critical columns falls below the 95% or if there are duplicate keys. How to implement this in a managed way on the pipeline?
options: Trust in end-consumer validation
Rules of AWS Glue Data Quality (DQDL) evaluated in the pipeline, conditioning the publication stage to the result
Increase Firehose buffer
A manual conference sheet
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: pushing bad data to the consumer destroys trust in the data. Glue Data Quality expresses the rules (IsComplete, Uniqueness, etc.) in DQDL, generates score and result by rule — the pipeline (Step Functions/Workflow) publishes only if it happens. C) Incorrect: buffer does not validate content. D) Incorrect: manual does not scale or rotate at 3h in the morning.

questions.text: Malformed records are making the transformation Lambda of the Kinesis Data Firehose fail. The team needs to ensure that these records are NOT lost for further analysis. What native behavior of Firehose attends?
options: Firehose for the entire stream until manual intervention
Records with processing failure are delivered in a prefix of ERRO no bucket S3 (processing-failed), preserving them for reprocessing
Records return to producer
Firehose silently discards records with error
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: stream continues to flow to valid records. B) Correct: Firehose records failed (and error metadata) on an error path in S3 — the pattern to debug and reprocess. C) Incorrect: there is no return to the producer. D) Incorrect: Firehose does not silently rule out transformation failures..

questions.text: Night loads via COPY no Redshift sometimes fail by corrupted files, aborting the entire batch. The team agrees to tolerate a small number of bad lines and wants to inspect them later. COPY Help?
options: MAXERROR to tolerate N errors and system tables (STL_LOAD_ERRORS) to inspect rejected lines
IGNOREHEADER 1 resolve any error
Roll COPY twice.
Disable file compression
questions.explanation: A) Correction: MAXERROR allows the load to continue to tolerate up to N bad lines, and STL_LOAD_ERRORS records the reason and content of each rejection.: IGNOREHEADER only jump headers. C) Incorrect: repeat load repeats error. D) Incorrect: compression is not the cause of corrupted lines.

questions.text: When choosing between AWS Step Functions and Amazon MWAA (Airflow) to orchestrate pipelines, which decision criterion is CORRETO?
options: Step Functions is serverless, natively integrates services AWS and shines in event-oriented flows; MWAA makes sense when the team already dominates Airflow/DAGs in Python or needs the ecosystem of Airflow operators
MWAA is always cheaper than Step Functions
Step Functions does not support error treatment
MWAA is serverless and has no fixed cost
questions.explanation: A) Correct: this is the real trade-off — native/serverless/events (Step Functions) (b) Incorrect: MWAA It's costing. FIXO Environment 24/7; Step Functions paid for by transition. C) Incorrect: Retry/Catch are strong points of Step Functions. D) Incorrect: or MWAA keeps environment continuously provided.

questions.text: Scheduled consultations of Athena which feed reports have started to fail intermittently. Where are the status, error and bytes information scanned from CADA diagnostic consultation execution?
options: No. AWS Configure
In the history of consultations of the Athena (console/API) and the workgroup metrics in the CloudWatch
No. S3 Inventory
Only in the administrator's email
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: Config does not record query executions. B) Correct: the Athena keeps history by query (state, error, bytes, time) and publishes metrics by workgroup in CloudWatch — the basis of the diagnosis and alarms. C) Incorrect: Inventory lists objects of the S3. D) Incorrect: no report by native email.

questions.text: The team of marketing analysts can see the `clients' table of the data lake, but NOT the cpf columns and income. Engineers see everything. How to implement this control in the ecosystem Athena/Glue?
options: Create two bucks and duplicate data
Bucket policy denying columns
An Excel view
Permissions to COLUNA no AWS Lake Training (column-level security) by group/role
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: duplicate data creates divergence and doubles cost/governance. B) Incorrect: Bucket policy operates on objects/prefixes, not in columns. C) Incorrect: customer control is not security. D) Correct: Lake Formation grants access by table and column (including column exclusion) by main — Athena automatically respect.

questions.text: Dozens of banks and hundreds of data lake tables need consistent permissions by area (financial, marketing, engineering), and granting table table became unsustainable. What mechanism of Lake Formation scale this governance?
options: One IAM policy by table
LF-Tags (tag-based access control): classifying features with tags and granting permissions to TAGS, not to individual resources
Increase the number of administrators
Share credentials by area
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: one policy per table is exactly what does not scale. B) Correct: with TBAC, resources receive LF-Tags (e.g. area=financial) and permissions are granted to tag — new tables with tag inherit access automatically. C) Incorrect: more admins = more manual work and risk. D) Incorrect: share credentials violates everything.

questions.text: By regulatory requirement, a cluster Amazon Redshift needs rest encryption with customer-managed key and the possibility to audit each use of the key.?
options: Encryption only in snapshots
SSL only in connections
Cluster encryption with AWS KMS using a customer managed key
Strong password in admin user
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: the requirement is the whole cluster, not just snapshots. B) Incorrect: SSL (c) Correct: or Redshift encrypt cluster and snapshots with KMS; with CMK own, each use appears in CloudTrail and access to the key is controlled by policy. D) Incorrect: password is authentication, not cryptography at rest.

questions.text: The company wants to automatically detect data uploads with PII in data lake and be warned to act. Which managed architecture implements this?
options: Lock all uploads
Weekly manual revision of the newsletters
GuardDuty with malware protection
Amazon Macie with automated discovery + findings sent to EventBridge, activating notification/remediation
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: blocking everything makes the business impossible. B) Incorrect: manual does not scale and arrives late. C) Incorrect: GuardDuty detects AMERICAS, does not classify PII. D) Correct: or Macie classification PII continuously and publishes findings in EventBridge — of which, SNS for alert or Lambda/Step Functions for automatic object quarantine.

questions.text: Jobs of AWS Glue connect on a bench RDS for extraction. The password needs to exit the code, be encrypted and rotated periodically without breaking jobs.?
options: Password in a .txt file in S3 with ACL Private
Save password to Secrets Manager with automatic rotation, and the Glue Connection/job looking for the secret in runtime via IAM
Fixed environment variable in the job
Encode the password to base64 in the script
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: Bucket file is neither safe nor rotates. B) Correct: Secrets Manager encrypt, control by IAM, (c) Incorrect: fixed envelope does not rotate and leaks into logs/console..

questions.text: A partner needs to consult UMA specific table of the company's date lake from the account itself AWS of it, without receiving credentials from the data-owner account.?
options: Export table by e-mail weekly
Make the public bucket with URL secret
Cross-account sharing via Lake Formation (grant to external account), with partner consulting with Athena on her account
Send key accesses to the dowry account by email
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: manual export loses governance, timeliness and audit trail. B) Incorrect: 'URL C) Correct: the Lake Formation grants cross-account permissions at the table/column level; the partner accepts sharing (RAM) and consultation with the own identities, all audited. D) Incorrect: sending credentials is the worst security scenario.

questions.text: The consultations of the Athena on logs JSON They're expensive and slow. DUAS Do optimizations drastically reduce bytes scanned by query? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Convert data to Parquet with compression
Partition by date and filter by partition columns
Use SELECT * instead of specific columns
Increase the number of bucks
Enable MFA Delete

C) Incorrect: SELECT * is the opposite — scans all columns. D) Incorrect: the quantity of buckets does not affect the scanning.: MFA Delete is protection against exclusion.

questions.text: Which ones DUAS statements on the components of the AWS Glue Are they correct? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Data Catalog is the central metastore shared by Athena, EMR and Redshift Spectrum
The Glue requires the provision and administration of a Spark cluster of its own
The Job Bookmarks allow incremental processing, tracking what has already been processed
The Crawlers perform the transformations of ETL
DataBrew replaces Data Catalog
questions.explanation: A) Correct: a single metadata catalogue serves all analytical tools — the heart of the lake. Glue is serverless — Spark infrastructure is managed by AWS. C) Correct: bookmarks avoid reprocessing old data for each execution. D) Incorrect: crawlers DESCOBREM and catalogue; the transformations are the JOBS. E) Incorrect: DataBrew is visual data preparation; the catalog remains the Data Catalog.

questions.text: A Daily Pipeline (Glue + Step Functions) needs OBSERVABILIDADE minimum production. DUAS Do configurations form this base? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Disable Logs to Save
Rule of EventBridge for states FAILED publishing alert no SNS
Check dashboard manually when someone remembers
Alarms of the CloudWatch on key metrics (job errors, anonymous duration, IteratorAge of streams)
Roll the pipeline twice to ensure
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: no logs no diagnosis. B) Correct: failure turns notification in real time to the team. C) Incorrect: memory monitoring is the anti-standard. D) Correct: alarms about error/duration/lag detect degradation before the user. E) Incorrect: re-execution blinds duplicates cost and can duplicate data.

questions.text: Which ones DUAS practices follow the principle of MENOR PRIVILEGY in data pipelines? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: A single admin roll shared by all pipelines
Each job/pipeline with its own IAM Role, restricted to the buckets/tables you really use
Long-term credentials embedded in scripts
Permission s3:* in Resource:* to simplify
Read access of analysts granted by table/column via Lake Formation
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: shared admin is the opposite of the lowest privilege. B) Correct: roles per pipeline limit damage radius and facilitate audit. C) Incorrect: fixed credentials in code are advertised leak. D) Incorrect: total curinga is the definition of excess privilege. E) Correct: granularity table/column gives each team only what is needed.
